div.h1: Engineers who maintain what they sell
div.p: Working with Odoo since 2015, from Ribeirão Preto, across Brazil, and inside the global community that maintains the platform.

div.h2: What we do, and for whom
div.p: We implement, develop and sustain Odoo Community with the community module ecosystem and the Brazilian fiscal localisation. Most of our clients run Community rather than Enterprise, which is unusual in this market and entirely deliberate.

We are engineers first. The same people who answer your support ticket are the people who maintain modules that thousands of companies install, which is why we can say what a platform will and will not do without checking with anyone.
We work remotely across Brazil, and we are increasingly asked to work outside it by other members of the community.
Companies from roughly twenty to three hundred users, with a real operation, a decision maker involved and some appetite for changing a process when the standard is better than the habit.

Below that size, the vendor's own packaged offer is usually a better fit and we will tell you so on the first call. We are also the wrong choice for anyone who wants the cheapest possible quote — that is not the trade we are making.
Verify us before you trust us. Our work is public.
Founder. Ninth in the world in the 2025 community contributor index, with 794 reviews on other people's contributions.
Twentieth in the world in the same index. Concentrated on the Brazilian fiscal localisation.

The rest of the team is on our organisation page , and the ranking is in a public dataset anyone can read. The index ranks individuals, so we say two of our engineers are in the top twenty, and never that the company is ninth.

p.a: What we do inside the community

div.p: Sound architecture, sustainable code, no technical debt handed to you quietly. We extend rather than modify, we test what we build, and nobody merges their own work.
Predictability and governance, of delivery, of cost and of operation. We would rather lose a deal by saying a number early than win it and argue about scope later.
Process before technology, and long term continuity. Go live is not the finish line; it is the point at which the real questions start arriving.

div.h2: Why we do not sell implementations abroad
div.p: An implementation needs somebody who understands the local tax rules, the local accounting practice and the local business habits. We have that for Brazil and we do not have it anywhere else, so selling it would be dishonest.

What travels well is engineering: code, reviews, upgrades and the discipline of reducing what an installation carries. That is what we offer, usually as a subcontractor to a local partner who owns the client relationship.

Mainly other members of the community — integrators in Europe who already know our names from the reviews on their own pull requests, and who need engineering capacity that will not embarrass them in front of a client.
Also companies running Odoo in a market without heavy tax localisation requirements, where the work is genuinely about the platform rather than about local compliance.
We work in Portuguese, English and Spanish, in a timezone that overlaps most of the European working day.

t.t-value: 'Need engineering capacity on an Odoo project?'
'Tell us what the work is and who owns the client. We answer with a capacity, a rate and a start date.'

div.p: Including the ones with uncomfortable answers.
Is Odoo Community really free?

The software is, under the LGPL. The work of implementing and maintaining it is not. Community trades a licence fee for service cost, and on a small team that is not growing, Enterprise can be the cheaper answer. How the numbers compare .
What do I lose by not taking Enterprise?

Studio, the native mobile app, the live spreadsheet, marketing automation, online appointments, the shop floor tablet screen, and a support contract signed by Odoo S.A. Those are real losses and we list them row by row .
Do you implement Enterprise too?
Yes, and we recommend it when it is the right answer. We are not interested in selling you the edition that suits our positioning.
Can I move from Community to Enterprise later, or back?

Community to Enterprise is straightforward. The other direction means replacing the Enterprise-only apps you adopted with community equivalents, which is a project. Worth knowing before you choose, not after.
Does Odoo handle Brazilian fiscal documents?

NF-e, CT-e and MDF-e are issued natively by the community localisation, with the taxes calculated inside Odoo and no external paid tax service required. NFS-e depends on your municipality. SPED, ECD and ECF are generated from the accounting data and validated in a specialist tool. Payroll is not solved by any Odoo edition. That is the complete answer, and it is the same answer on every page of this site .
Will I need to buy a separate tax product?
For the documents above, no. Some companies still keep a specialist tool for fiscal file validation and their accountant's workflow, which is a reasonable choice rather than a gap.
What about the tax reform?

Being built upstream, in public, for a transition running to 2033, and arriving on the current versions first. If you are on an older Odoo, that is now an upgrade decision. Start with a readiness audit .
Can Odoo run my payroll?
No, and neither can Enterprise. We integrate a specialist payroll provider and post the accounting entries. Anyone telling you otherwise has not run a Brazilian payroll.
How much does an implementation cost?

It depends on process complexity, your fiscal profile, integrations and how much data you migrate — not primarily on head count. Comparable companies invest around one percent of annual revenue in their management platform. The full breakdown, with a benchmark you can check us against .
Will you quote a fixed price for the whole project?
Not before discovery. Anyone who does is either padding the number heavily or planning to argue about scope later. We quote discovery at a fixed price, and each phase after it separately.
What should I budget after go live?
Fifteen to twenty five percent of the implementation cost per year for evolution and support. A project budgeted with nothing reserved for the year after go live will stall twelve months in.
Is there a minimum engagement?

For implementations, effectively yes: below roughly twenty users the economics rarely work in your favour and we will say so. The small fixed-scope services — second opinion, readiness audit, pre-upgrade diagnostic — have no minimum.
How long does an implementation take?

A focused operation with a simple fiscal profile is weeks per phase. A multi-company industrial operation issuing documents across several states is months. The biggest variable is your team's availability, not ours.
Do I get the source code?
Yes, in a repository you can access from the first week, not as a zip file at the end. Including the exit plan .
What is your support response time?

One business hour for a stopped operation, four for a degraded core process, one business day for normal, three for low. Response means a person engaged, not an automated acknowledgement. The plans in full .
Can you take over an Odoo somebody else implemented?
Yes, and it is how a large share of our clients arrive. It starts with an assessment: either a second opinion or a rescue , depending on how bad it is.
What happens if we stop working together?
You already hold the repository, the deployment recipe and your data, so nothing has to be handed over. There is a notice period in the contract, in both directions.
Are community modules safe to run in production?

The ones we deploy are. They live in public repositories with a review process, automated tests and named maintainers — and we are among the people doing the reviewing. We choose which ones to install, and that judgement is a large part of what you are paying for.
Who maintains them if the author disappears?
The association, through the repository maintainers. That is precisely the difference from a module sitting in one supplier's private repository.
Are you an official Odoo partner?
Our credential is the contribution record, which is public and checkable: two of our engineers rank in the global top twenty of the 2025 community contributor index. With a link to the dataset .
